title: SKU-aware quant presets and cache-fallback matrix with unit-econ simulator
author: Anya Kapoor
description: Motivation: We need safer, workload-aware defaults for quantization and caching that map to customer SKUs (hardware tiers and capacity classes) so teams get predictable unit economics without manual tuning. This PR introduces a SKU-to-quant preset catalog, a cache-fallback degradation matrix (safe degradation paths when a preferred preset is unavailable), and a lightweight unit-economics simulator that runs on representative traces to estimate per-token cost/latency impact for each SKU/preset. Summary: - Add configs/quant_presets/sku_catalog.yml that encodes hardware SKUs -> quant profiles + recommended batching/cache settings. - Introduce a degradation matrix (configs/cache_fallbacks.yml) which defines safe downgrade steps (e.g., 8bit -> 6bit fallback with KV-cache warmup heuristics) and associated quality checkpoints. - New CLI tool tools/cost_simulator (go) that ingests a request trace, applies cataloged presets, simulates batching/caching and outputs estimated latency, GPU-time, and token-cost deltas. - Integrate telemetry: econ.simulation.* metrics and an audit event when an automatic fallback is triggered at runtime. - Platform hooks: add a new routing option sku_based_defaults in the serving config; when enabled, the router will attach the appropriate preset to a request. Design decisions: - Catalog as YAML so SRE/solutions can patch presets per-customer without code changes. - Simulator is intentionally approximate (fast single-pass sim using empirical per-token kernels) — it is meant for comparative profiling, not absolute billing. - Degradation matrix includes explicit quality checkpoints (prompt tests) and a configurable safe_threshold to avoid silent regressions. Testing & rollout: - Unit tests for catalog parsing, fallback selector, and simulator core (fast-path and edge cases). - Integration tests: small end-to-end using a sampled trace and a local serving runtime (mocked kernels) to verify metrics emission and fallback path. - Canary rollout: default off; enable sku_based_defaults for Dedicated tier in canary region for 48h and monitor econ.simulation.delta and quality.regression.* alarms. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: quant fallbacks cause regressions in specific prompts. Mitigation: quality checkpoints and auto-disable if regression > safe_threshold. - Risk: incorrect catalog mapping for custom hardware SKUs. Mitigation: lifecycle hooks for operators to override mappings, and a validation command (tools/cost_simulator --validate-catalog). Related: builds on prior work for prefilling/batching heuristics (see ENG-1467) and compliments the economizer recommendations. Checklist: - [x] Catalog format defined - [x] Simulator CLI implemented - [x] Degradation matrix schema + validator - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry hooks - [x] Docs updated (docs/ops/sku-quant-presets.md)
